preamble: Fortition of the lateral approximant [l] to the voiceless lateral fricative [ɬ] is best known from Welsh, where inherited and borrowed word-initial *l- became ll [ɬ] (Proto-Celtic *lindos > llyn, Latin liber > llyfr), while Irish kept [l]. In Greenlandic, geminate /lː/ is realized as the voiceless fricative [ɬː], as in illu [iɬːu] 'house' and kalaallisut [kalaːɬːisʉt].

examples.note: Via Proto-Brythonic *llɨnn; word-initial *l- regularly became [ɬ]. Compare Irish leann 'ale', which keeps [l].
Latin loans with initial l- also show the change (Middle Welsh llyuyr); compare Breton levr.
Geminate /l/ is realized as a voiceless lateral fricative.
